lessons.title: Integers and the number line
lessons.objective: Compare and add negative and positive numbers.

introduce.text: Numbers can be below zero. They are called negative numbers: -1, -2, -3 and so on. On the number line they sit to the left of 0, and the ones to the right are positive.
introduce.speech: Numbers can be below zero. They are called negative numbers: negative 1, negative 2, negative 3 and so on. On the number line they sit to the left of 0, and the ones to the right are positive.

introduce.text: Numbers further to the right are greater. So 3 is greater than -2, and -2 is greater than -8. Temperatures work the same way: -8 degrees is colder than -2 degrees.
introduce.speech: Numbers further to the right are greater. So 3 is greater than negative 2, and negative 2 is greater than negative 8. Temperatures work the same way: negative 8 degrees is colder than negative 2 degrees.

demonstrate.text: To add a positive number, move right. Take -7 + 3: start at -7 and move 3 steps right. You land on -4.
demonstrate.speech: To add a positive number, move right. Take negative 7 plus 3: start at negative 7 and move 3 steps right. You land on negative 4.

demonstrate.text: To subtract a positive number, move left. Take 2 - 5: start at 2 and move 5 steps left. You pass 0 and land on -3.
demonstrate.speech: To subtract a positive number, move left. Take 2 minus 5: start at 2 and move 5 steps left. You pass 0 and land on negative 3.

guided.speech: Which is the smallest: negative 2, 5 or negative 9?
hints: Mark the three numbers on a number line. The smallest is furthest to the left.
The numbers in order are -9, -2, 5. The one furthest left is -9.

wrong_feedback.-2: -2 is closest to 0, so it is not the smallest. Negatives get smaller as the size grows.
wrong_feedback.5: 5 is positive. Every negative number is smaller than every positive number.

guided.explanation: -9 is the smallest, because it is furthest left on the number line.

hints: Start at the first number on the number line. Adding moves you right.
Start at -4 and move 7 steps right. You land on 3.

wrong_feedback.-3: The size is right but the sign is wrong. Check which side of 0 you finish on.
wrong_feedback.11: You added the sizes and ignored the signs. A negative number moves you the other way.

guided.explanation: -4 + 7 = 3. Start at -4 and move 7 steps right.

hints: Picture both on the number line. The number further to the right is greater.
-2 is further right than -6, so -6 < -2.

wrong_feedback.>: That compares the sizes only. For negatives the bigger size is further left, so -6 is the smaller number.
wrong_feedback.=: -6 and -2 are different points on the number line, so they are not equal.

practice.explanation: -6 < -2, because -2 is further right on the number line.

hints: Start at the first number on the number line. Subtracting moves you left.
Start at 5 and move 8 steps left. You land on -3.

wrong_feedback.3: The size is right but the sign is wrong. Check which side of 0 you finish on.
wrong_feedback.13: Subtracting means moving left on the number line, not right.

practice.explanation: 5 - 8 = -3. Start at 5 and move 8 steps left.

practice.speech: At night the temperature is negative 3 degrees. It rises by 8 degrees. What is the temperature now?

wrong_feedback.=: -9 and -5 are different points on the number line, so they are not equal.

check.explanation: -9 < -5, because -5 is further right on the number line.

explain.text: Another way: think of a lift. Ground floor is 0, floors above are positive, floors in the basement are negative. Basement 2 is the same place as -2.
explain.speech: Another way: think of a lift. Ground floor is 0, floors above are positive, floors in the basement are negative. Basement 2 is the same place as negative 2.

explain.text: Going up adds, going down subtracts. Start in basement 4 (-4) and go up 6 floors. -4 + 6 = 2, which is floor 2.

explain.text: The smaller number is the one lower down. Basement 9 (-9) is lower than basement 3 (-3), so -9 < -3. A deeper basement means a smaller number.
explain.speech: The smaller number is the one lower down. Basement 9 (negative 9) is lower than basement 3 (negative 3), so negative 9 is less than negative 3. A deeper basement means a smaller number.

check.explanation: 0 > -4, because 0 is further right on the number line.

lessons.title: Order of operations
lessons.objective: Evaluate expressions in the correct order.

introduce.text: When a sum has more than one operation, the order matters. Take 6 + 4 x 3. If you go left to right you get 30, but the correct answer is 18.
introduce.speech: When a sum has more than one operation, the order matters. Take 6 plus 4 times 3. If you go left to right you get 30, but the correct answer is 18.

introduce.text: The rule: brackets first, then x and ÷, then + and -. In 6 + 4 x 3 the multiplication goes first: 4 x 3 = 12, then 6 + 12 = 18.
introduce.speech: The rule: brackets first, then times and ÷, then plus and -. In 6 plus 4 times 3 the multiplication goes first: 4 times 3 equals 12, then 6 plus 12 equals 18.

demonstrate.text: Brackets change the order. In (8 + 4) x 3 do the bracket first: 8 + 4 = 12. Then 12 x 3 = 36. Without the brackets, 8 + 4 x 3 would be 20.
demonstrate.speech: Brackets change the order. In (8 plus 4) times 3 do the bracket first: 8 plus 4 equals 12. Then 12 times 3 equals 36. Without the brackets, 8 plus 4 times 3 would be 20.

demonstrate.text: Try 20 - 12 ÷ 4. Division goes before subtraction: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Then 20 - 3 = 17. Doing 20 - 12 first would wrongly give 2.
demonstrate.speech: Try 20 minus 12 divided by 4. Division goes before subtraction: 12 divided by 4 equals 3. Then 20 minus 3 equals 17. Doing 20 minus 12 first would wrongly give 2.

guided.prompt: Which part do you work out first in 9 - 2 x 3?
guided.speech: Which part do you work out first in 9 minus 2 times 3?
options: Any part, the order does not matter

x and ÷ are worked out before + and -. So 2 x 3 comes first.

wrong_feedback.Any part, the order does not matter: The order does matter. 6 + 4 x 3 is 18, but working left to right would give 30.

guided.explanation: In 9 - 2 x 3 you work out 2 x 3 first. x and ÷ are worked out before + and -.

lessons.title: Fractions with unlike denominators
lessons.objective: Add and subtract fractions with different bottoms.

introduce.text: You can only add fractions when the pieces are the same size. 1/2 and 1/3 have different bottoms, so the pieces are different sizes. First we make the bottoms equal.
introduce.speech: You can only add fractions when the pieces are the same size. 1/2 and 1/3 have different bottoms, so the pieces are different sizes. First we make the bottoms equal.

introduce.text: The common bottom of 2 and 3 is 6. 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6. Now both are sixths, so we can add the tops.
introduce.speech: The common bottom of 2 and 3 is 6. 1/2 equals 3/6 and 1/3 equals 2/6. Now both are sixths, so we can add the tops.

demonstrate.text: Add: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. Only the tops are added. The bottom stays 6, because the pieces are still sixths.
demonstrate.speech: Add: 1/2 plus 1/3 equals 3/6 plus 2/6 equals 5/6. Only the tops are added. The bottom stays 6, because the pieces are still sixths.

demonstrate.text: Subtract the same way: 3/4 - 1/6. The smallest common bottom is 12. 3/4 = 9/12 and 1/6 = 2/12. So 9/12 - 2/12 = 7/12.
demonstrate.speech: Subtract the same way: 3/4 minus 1/6. The smallest common bottom is 12. 3/4 equals 9/12 and 1/6 equals 2/12. So 9/12 minus 2/12 equals 7/12.

hints: Make the bottoms equal first. Then add only the tops.
1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6. Then 3 + 2 = 5 over 6, and simplify.

wrong_feedback.2/5: You added the tops and added the bottoms. The bottoms must be made equal first.
wrong_feedback.1/3: You added the tops but did not change them when the bottoms changed. Convert both fractions first.

guided.explanation: 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, after making both bottoms 6.

guided.prompt: Which is the smallest common denominator of 4 and 6?
guided.speech: Which is the smallest common denominator of 4 and 6?
hints: List the multiples of each number. Look for the first one they share.
Multiples of 4 and of 6: the first one in both lists is 12.

wrong_feedback.24: 24 works, but it is not the smallest. Look for a smaller number that both 4 and 6 divide into.
wrong_feedback.6: 6 is not a multiple of both 4 and 6.

guided.explanation: The smallest common denominator of 4 and 6 is 12, their lowest common multiple.

3/4 = 9/12 and 1/6 = 2/12. Then 9 - 2 = 7 over 12, and simplify.

wrong_feedback.1/12: You subtracted the tops but did not change them when the bottoms changed. Convert both fractions first.

lessons.title: Fraction multiplication
lessons.objective: Multiply fractions: a part of a part.

introduce.text: Multiplying fractions means taking a part of a part. 2/3 of 3/4 asks: if you have 3/4 of a bar, how much is 2/3 of that piece?
introduce.speech: Multiplying fractions means taking a part of a part. 2/3 of 3/4 asks: if you have 3/4 of a bar, how much is 2/3 of that piece?

introduce.text: The rule is simple. Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms, then simplify. 2 x 3 = 6 and 3 x 4 = 12, so the answer is 6/12.
introduce.speech: The rule is simple. Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms, then simplify. 2 times 3 equals 6 and 3 times 4 equals 12, so the answer is 6/12.

demonstrate.text: Do it again: 3/4 x 2/5. Tops: 3 x 2 = 6. Bottoms: 4 x 5 = 20. So 6/20, which simplifies to 3/10 (divide both by 2).
demonstrate.speech: Do it again: 3/4 times 2/5. Tops: 3 times 2 equals 6. Bottoms: 4 times 5 equals 20. So 6/20, which simplifies to 3/10 (divide both by 2).

demonstrate.text: For a fraction of a whole number, divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top. 3/4 of 24: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, and 6 x 3 = 18.
demonstrate.speech: For a fraction of a whole number, divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top. 3/4 of 24: 24 divided by 4 equals 6, and 6 times 3 equals 18.

hints: Multiply the two tops, then multiply the two bottoms, then simplify.
2 x 3 = 6 and 3 x 4 = 12, so 6/12, which simplifies to 1/2.

wrong_feedback.6/7: You added the bottoms. To multiply, multiply the bottoms.

hints: Divide by the bottom number first, then multiply by the top number.
